newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor to propose 1 wk clothing tax moratorium.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor to propose 1 wk clothing tax moratorium.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said Wednesday he planned to ask the City Council to approve a one-week moratorium in January on sales taxes for clothing and shoes that cost $500 or less.

The mayor's proposal, which aims to encourage shoppers to buy more clothes, matches a one-week moratorium for the state's four percent sales tax that was included in its 1997 fiscal budget for the week of Martin Luther King Jr's birthday.

While Giuliani, who made the announcement at a Crain's New York Business breakfast here, had suggested he would make a similar proposal in the budget for the 1997 fiscal year that was approved in June, the plan was not part of his final budget.

But City Council sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the council was expected to approve as soon as this afternoon the one-week moratorium on the city's four percent sales taxes on clothing and footwear. The break, described as a belated holiday gift for retailers and shoppers, would run from January 18 to January 24.
And Giuliani said he would continue to push for lower sales taxes. "That's something that we will continue to try to do. You work at these things with the City Council."

As part of his speech, the mayor, who is trying to get the City Council to allow so-called superstores, which are large retail outlets, to be built in industrial areas, highlighted the importance of the retail sector to New York City.

Saying that on a percentage basis the city since 1961 had lost as many if not more jobs in the retail industry as in manufacturing, he stressed the potential riches the city might gain by concentrating on this sector.

The mayor, noting the city this year may draw up to 28 million tourists, added opening up the zoning laws to allow for superstores could help the city "regain some $3.5 billion of retail sales that moves across the borders of the city."
However, members of the City Council have objected to loosening the zoning stores because small businesses are afraid the new competition will drive them out of business.
